module_summary: The menu-side RetroAchievements stack plus the plain-HTTP clock fetch. nettime.cpp (every build) reads an HTTP Date header to set the clock. rahash.cpp computes the rcheevos PS2/PS1 image hash with its own ISO9660 walker over files, VCDs, HDL partitions and the disc drive; ranet.cpp talks UDP (RAP1/RAQ1/RAG1, CADQ2) and HTTP to the xeRAbora/Caduceus PC, fetches the watch list in chunks and saves it; rabadge.cpp caches the game-list badge; rahunt.cpp formats the locked-achievement list for the in-game menu; rapopslaunch.cpp writes the POPStarter MODULE_9.IRX with a filled config block. ratls_ps2.cpp is the PS2 glue (DNS, BIO, clock, entropy, CA roots) for mbedTLS used by RA HTTPS and the self-updater. ranet/rabadge/rahash/rawatch, rahunt and rapopslaunch are compiled only in RA editions (tools/build_edition.py:96-98); ratls_ps2 in RA or updater builds (:116,:139).

findings.title: Ranet, RaBadge, RaHash and RaWatch are single-instance classes wrapped by a full layer of free forwarder functions
findings.problem: Each class has exactly one object (gRanet, gRaBadge, static gRaHash, gRaWatch) and every product caller uses the C-style free functions, which only forward to that object (13 in ranet.cpp, 2 in rabadge.cpp, 6 plus disc_read_at in rahash.cpp, 8 in rawatch.cpp). The extern instance declarations in the headers are used by no other file. Two layers do the job of one; RaHash's comment even admits the class only exists in the .cpp because a test strips includes.
findings.fix: Keep the free API that callers use. Turn each class into file-static state plus static functions in its .cpp, delete the class declarations, the extern instance lines and the forwarders, and name the former methods after the free functions (e.g. RaHash::hashDisc becomes raHashDisc, discReadAt becomes disc_read_at). Update the host tests that stub Ranet:: and RaWatch:: members by name to stub the static functions instead.
findings.benefit: ~200 lines removed (INFERRED: ~60 forwarder lines in ranet.cpp, ~70 in rahash.cpp class+forwarders, ~40 in rawatch.cpp, ~25 in rabadge, header decls). ~30 forwarders of ~8-16 bytes each, ~0.3 KB in RA ELFs (INFERRED, not measured).
findings.evidence: Grep \bg(Ranet|RaBadge|RaHash|RaWatch)\b over src/RiptOPL: only the definitions, the header externs and the forwarders in ranet.cpp:148-203, rabadge.cpp:50-59, rahash.cpp:115-152, rawatch.cpp:32-71. Every forwarder has product callers (achievements.cpp, supportbase.cpp, host.cpp, menusys.cpp, guisettings.cpp, rapopslaunch.cpp, ratls_ps2.cpp, discsupport.cpp). Class names appear in tests: .github/scripts/test_caduceus_browser.py:160-194, test_ra_chunk_integrity.py:37-114, test_ra_xerabora_browser.py:336-445, test_network_parity_922.py:37-55, test_ra_runtime_budget.py:188-190, test_ra_menu_link.py:187 (these stub or extract members by signature, so they need editing). rahash's tests (test_ra_disc.py, test_ra_ps1.py) use the free names only.

findings.title: raVcdBootName / RaHash::vcdBootName has no product caller (test-only)
findings.problem: raVcdBootName is declared, defined and forwarded, but the only caller in the repo is .github/scripts/test_ra_ps1.py:139. Its PSX.EXE fallback (839-842) is a second copy of the one in hashPsx (773-780); hashVcd already returns the boot name through its boot argument.
findings.fix: Delete raVcdBootName, RaHash::vcdBootName and the prototype; let test_ra_ps1.py check the boot name that raHashVcd fills in.
findings.benefit: ~27 lines removed. Non-static and unreferenced, so --gc-sections (ps2.yaml:649) already drops it: no ELF change (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Grep -i vcdBootName over src/RiptOPL: test_ra_ps1.py:139, rahash.h:22, rahash.cpp:89,142,144,826. No match in src/ outside rahash.cpp, none in docs. ps2.yaml:645,649 compile with -ffunction-sections and link with --gc-sections.

findings.title: rahash.cpp: the MD5(name || extent) chunk loop is written three times
findings.problem: hashBootExec and hashPsx carry the same 20-line block (md5_init, append name, read RA_HASH_CHUNK pieces through readAt into g_chunk, md5_finish, md5_hex); hashDisc repeats it a third time over a plain fd, which is exactly what readAt does for an RA_SRC_ISO source (lseek64 + read).
findings.fix: Keep one private helper md5Extent(src, name, off, size, out33) with the loop, call it from hashBootExec and hashPsx, and have hashDisc call it with RaSrc{fd, RA_SRC_ISO} at offset 0.
findings.justification: Three copies of the same loop exist; one helper replaces them and removes code overall.
findings.benefit: ~30 lines removed (INFERRED: three ~20-line blocks become one helper plus three calls). A few hundred bytes of .text in RA ELFs (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read rahash.cpp:504-553, 620-658, 765-824 and readAt at 388-401. The step strings differ only at the end (5-hashed-directly vs 5-psx-hashed); grep shows no test matches on those strings.

findings.title: NIC-reserved predicate, peek-then-recv rule, hostent and deadline check written up to three times in nettime, ratls_ps2 and ranet
findings.problem: The 'UDP transport owns or is chosen for the NIC' expression exists in ranet.cpp:229-230, ratls_ps2.cpp:151-152 and nettime.cpp:138-139; the peek/shorten-to-48-byte-tail recv in ranet.cpp:1074-1079, ratls_ps2.cpp:158-163 and inline in nettime.cpp:110-119; struct hostent twice; the elapsed-clock check three times. ratls_ps2 carries an #ifdef split (137-165) only because ranet.cpp is RA-only, and ratlsNicBusy -> ratlsNicReserved -> raNetNicReserved -> Ranet::nicReserved is four hops.
findings.fix: Define netNicReserved(), netTcpRecv() and the hostent struct once in an always-compiled network file (nettime.cpp or ethsupport.cpp, with prototypes in its header). Make Ranet::nicReserved use it, delete Ranet::tcpRecv, raNetTcpRecv, raNetNicReserved, the ratls_ps2 #ifdef block and ratlsNicBusy (selfupdate.cpp calls netNicReserved), and use netTcpRecv in nettime's loop.
findings.justification: The same three helpers are already written two or three times; moving one copy to a file every build compiles deletes the others and the RA/non-RA #ifdef split, so code shrinks overall.
findings.benefit: ~50 lines removed (INFERRED: ratls_ps2 137-165 and 260-264, one hostent, ranet forwarders and tcpRecv, nettime inline recv). Small .text saving in RA/updater ELFs (INFERRED, not measured).
findings.evidence: Grep 'gNetworkProtocol == NET_PROTO_UDPFSBD' over src: the NIC predicate only in nettime.cpp:139, ratls_ps2.cpp:152, ranet.cpp:229 (others are settings code). Grep 'got % 64 > 48' : nettime.cpp:117, ranet.cpp:1077, ratls_ps2.cpp:161. Grep '^struct hostent': nettime.cpp:31, ratls_ps2.cpp:41 (plus smstcpip-common.h, in-game stack). nettime.cpp is in the base riptopl source list (ps2.yaml:641); ranet only RA (build_edition.py:96-98); ratls_ps2 RA or updater (:116,:139). ratlsNicBusy caller: src/ui/selfupdate.cpp:215. Host tests naming raNetNicReserved/raNetTcpRecv: test_ratls_host.py:46, test_caduceus_browser.py:49,215, test_ra_xerabora_browser.py:85 need renaming.

findings.title: ratls_ps2.cpp: raHttpsGet and raHttpsDownload repeat the same clock/NIC/DNS/connect/deadline preamble; bio expiry ternary written three times
findings.problem: Lines 228-251 and 280-303 are the same 24 lines (raTlsClockOk, NIC check, gethostbyname, sockaddr fill for port 443, socket, connect, budget check); nettime.cpp:88-101 is a third copy of the DNS+connect part for port 80. bioSend and bioRecv each spell out 'bio->idle ? ratlsExpired(start, IDLE) : ratlsExpired(start)'.
findings.fix: Move the preamble into one static ratlsConnect(host, port, &bio) returning 0 or the RATLS_ERR_* code and call it from both entry points (nettime can share the DNS+connect part if finding 4's shared file hosts it). Fold the idle ternary into a one-line bioExpired(bio).
findings.justification: The block exists twice in the file (three times counting nettime); one helper removes code overall.
findings.benefit: ~25 lines removed (INFERRED: one 24-line copy becomes a call, three ternaries become calls). Small .text saving in RA+updater builds (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read ratls_ps2.cpp:174-312 and nettime.cpp:80-130. Duplicate-block lead dupes-blocks.tsv: ratls_ps2.cpp:231-246 == 283-298 (14 normalised lines), confirmed by reading; the only differences are raNetNicReserved vs ratlsNicReserved (equal in RA builds, see 138-141) and the later bio.idle setup at 304-305.

findings.title: ranet.cpp: the RAA1 OK reply is parsed twice by copy, re-scanned a second time in askPc, and trailing-space trimming is written three times
findings.problem: askPc (625-635) and xeraboraIdentify (1051-1059) carry the same five-or-three-number sscanf of 'RAA1 OK' plus title trim. askPc then sscanfs total/chunks again at 649 although bytes/ch from 625/629 already hold them. The 'while len>0 && s[len-1]==' '' trim appears at 603-604, 634-635 and 1057-1058.
findings.fix: One static raaParse(rx, &bytes, &chunks, &nach, &unlocked, &unsupported) returning the trimmed title, used by both; use its bytes/chunks in askPc instead of the second sscanf.
findings.justification: The parse exists twice; one helper replaces both and the redundant rescan.
findings.evidence: Read ranet.cpp:592-660 and 1020-1061; the comment at 1052 states the two shapes are 'the two reply shapes askPc accepts'. No existing trim helper in include/util.h (grep trim/strip: none).

findings.title: rahash.cpp: hex digit table and lowercase-hex validation each written twice
findings.problem: raVcdWatchKey re-declares the hex table and loop of md5_hex to produce 14 of its digits; raVcdGuardPath and raVcdValidContentHash run the same isxdigit/!isupper loop over 14 and 32 characters.
findings.fix: In raVcdWatchKey call md5_hex into a 33-byte temp and copy 14 characters after 'P'; give the two validators one shared lower-hex loop (or have raVcdGuardPath call a length-parameterised raVcdValidContentHash).
findings.justification: Reuses the existing md5_hex; the shared validator replaces two identical loops, so code shrinks.
